paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: Probing accuracy with reduced training data.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the probing accuracy of two multilingual BERT models—mBERT and XLM-R—as a function of training set size, ranging from approximately 125 to 2000 samples. The x-axis, labeled “Train size,” is linearly scaled from 0 to 2000 with major tick marks at intervals of 250. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” is linearly scaled from 80 to 94, with major tick marks at intervals of 2. Two distinct lines are plotted: mBERT is represented by a light blue line with ‘x’ markers, and XLM-R by a darker blue line with ‘x’ markers. Both models show increasing accuracy with larger training sizes, starting from low values and plateauing near the upper end of the x-axis. At a train size of 125, mBERT achieves approximately 83% accuracy while XLM-R reaches about 85%. By train size 2000, mBERT’s accuracy stabilizes near 90.5%, whereas XLM-R reaches approximately 91.8%. The gap in performance between the two models remains relatively consistent across training sizes, with XLM-R consistently outperforming mBERT.
